research_notes:
Here are the concise research notes for **Ticket to Ride: London** (Days of Wonder, 2019 English edition):

---

## Research Notes: Ticket to Ride: London (Days of Wonder, 2019)

---

### 1. Edition Identity


The English edition 2019 was published by Days of Wonder, with product code 720061, released July 2019.
 
The game was designed by Alan R. Moon, supports 2–4 players, and plays in 10–15 minutes.


---

### 2. Box Dimensions

**Internal dimensions: NOT FOUND.** No measured internal dimensions were located in any source.

**External dimensions (BGG versions page):** 
BGG lists the English edition 2019 (product code 720061) at **9.06 × 9.06 × 1.85 inches** (approximately **230 × 230 × 47 mm**).
 These are **external** dimensions reported by BGG and should not be treated as internal dimensions. No third-party measured internal dimensions were found. ⚠️ Do not invent internal clearance from these figures.

> **Note on other editions:** 
A 2021 English edition exists at a different size: 7.87 × 7.87 × 1.85 inches (200 × 200 × 47 mm).
 The user's specified edition is the 2019 release; use the 230 × 230 × 47 mm external figure for that edition only.

---

### 3. Component Inventory (as supplied — not modified)

| ID | Component | Qty | Dimensions (L × W × H mm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| component_1 | Board map | 1 | 236.6 × 168.9 × 4.0 |
| component_2 | Plastic Bus piece | 68 | 24.2 × 5.5 × 15.1 |
| component_3 | Transportation card | 44 | 67.7 × 44.1 × 0.4 |
| component_4 | Destination Ticket card | 20 | 69.0 × 43.5 × 0.4 |
| component_5 | Scoring Marker | 4 | ⌀14.7 × H13.3 (cylinder) |
| component_6 | Rule leaflet | 1 | 214.7 × 102.3 × 12.1 |

> **Cross-check against rulebook:** 
The official rulebook confirms the box contains: 44 Transportation cards (8 multi-coloured Bus cards and 6 cards each of blue, green, black, pink, yellow, and orange), 20 Destination Ticket cards, 4 Scoring Markers, plastic Buses, and the rule leaflet.
 The supplied inventory matches.

---

### 4. Component Ownership (Player-Assigned vs. Shared)

**Player-owned (assigned at setup, kept separate per player):**
- **Plastic Bus pieces:** 
Each player starts with a supply of 17 double-decker buses.
 With 68 total buses and up to 4 players, all 68 buses are pre-divided by colour into 4 player sets of 17. Each set belongs exclusively to one player throughout the game. *(Inference: buses must be separable by colour for setup and storage.)*
- **Scoring Markers:** One per player. 
Each player takes a set of coloured plastic buses along with its matching Scoring Marker.
 Each Scoring Marker is paired with and owned by its player.
- **Destination Ticket cards (hand):** 
Players must keep their Destination Ticket cards secret until the end of the game.
 Cards in hand are privately held by each player during play.

**Shared / common pool:**
- **Board map:** Placed centrally, shared by all.
- **Transportation cards:** 
Transportation cards are shuffled and two are dealt to each player as a starting hand; the remaining deck is placed near the board with five cards flipped face up.
 The deck and face-up display are a shared communal draw pool.
- **Destination Ticket cards (deck):** 
The Destination Ticket deck is placed next to the board
 as a shared draw pile.

---

### 5. Setup Distribution


Each player starts with a supply of 17 double-decker buses, two transportation cards in hand, and one or two destination tickets.


Specifically at setup:
- Each player receives their **17 coloured Bus pieces** and their **matching Scoring Marker**.
- 
Transportation cards are shuffled and two are dealt to each player as a starting hand.

- 
The Destination Ticket cards are shuffled and two are dealt to each player.
 
If a player chooses to keep only one, the returned card is placed on the bottom of the Destination Ticket deck.

- The remaining Transportation card deck and Destination Ticket deck both sit beside the board.

---

### 6. Gameplay Roles & Turn Actions


On a turn, a player either: (a) draws two transportation cards from the deck or the display of five face-up cards (or takes one face-up multi-coloured Bus card, which counts as all six colours); (b) claims a route on the board by discarding cards that match the colour of the route (with any matching set allowed for grey routes); or (c) draws two Destination Ticket cards and keeps at least one.



Ticket to Ride: London introduces Districts, which are represented on the board by numbers between each route.
 
A district consists of 2–4 locations, and a player scores 1–5 points for a district if they link all of its locations to one another with their buses.


All players share **identical roles** — there are no asymmetric player roles or special powers. This is a symmetric competitive game.

---

### 7. Deck Separation Requirements

There are **two distinct decks that must remain separate** at all times:

| Deck | Cards | Must Stay Separate From |
|---|---|---|
| **Transportation cards** | 44 cards | Destination Ticket cards |
| **Destination Ticket cards** | 20 cards | Transportation cards |

**Evidence:** 
The Transportation card deck is placed near the board with five cards flipped face up.
 
The Destination Ticket deck is placed separately next to the board.
 These two decks serve entirely different draw mechanics and must never be combined. Card dimensions are nearly identical (Transportation: 67.7 × 44.1 mm; Destination Ticket: 69.0 × 43.5 mm), so physical separation in storage is essential to prevent mixing.

> **Storage design implication:** These two decks should be stored in clearly separated compartments or bags, despite the cards being nearly the same size.

---

### 8. Simultaneous Independent Access Requirements

| Component | Simultaneous Access Needed? | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Plastic Buses (by colour) | **Yes** — each player accesses their own colour independently | Players place buses from their personal supply on their turn; each set must be accessible without disturbing others |
| Scoring Markers | **No** — placed on track at start, not repeatedly drawn from storage | Set out once at game start |
| Transportation card deck | **No** — one player draws per turn | Sequential, not simultaneous |
| Destination Ticket deck | **No** — one player draws per turn | Sequential, not simultaneous |
| Board map | **No** — shared, placed centrally | Single shared component |

**Key storage inference:** Bus pieces by colour need to be individually accessible (4 distinct colour sets). No component type demands simultaneous multi-player access from a central supply mid-game, beyond each player reaching their own bus stash.

---

### 9. Source URLs

- **Official London Rulebook PDF (Days of Wonder CDN):** `https://ncdn0.daysofwonder.com/tickettoride/fr/img/tt_ln_en_rules_2019-04.pdf`
- **Mirrored Rulebook PDF:** `https://cdn.1j1ju.com/medias/c7/f5/c0-ticket-to-ride-london-rulebook.pdf`
- **BGG Version Page (English 2019):** `https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgameversion/451831/english-edition-2019`
- **BGG Versions List:** `https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/276894/ticket-to-ride-london/versions`
- **Sleeve Your Games (component confirmation):** `https://www.sleeveyourgames.com/sleeves/6052/ticket-to-ride-london`

---

### 10. Known Facts vs. Inferences

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Component list and quantities | ✅ **Known** — confirmed against official rulebook |
| External box dimensions (230 × 230 × 47 mm) | ✅ **Known** — BGG versions page, cited as external |
| Internal box dimensions | ❌ **Not found** — no measured internal data located |
| Two decks must be separate | ✅ **Known** — confirmed by rulebook setup instructions |
| 17 buses per player, 4 players | ✅ **Known** — rulebook and multiple reviews confirm |
| Bus sets stored separately by colour | ⚠️ **Inference** — logical from player ownership; not explicitly stated as a storage rule |
| No simultaneous shared supply access mid-game | ⚠️ **Inference** — from turn structure (one action per turn, sequential) |
